elements.label: Figure 3.3: Populations by region, 2010-2020
elements.description:
Line chart. Y-axis: "Population (in millions)", scale 0 to 30 with gridlines at 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. X-axis: years 2010, 2012, 2014, 2016, 2018, 2020. Source note: World Bank staff calculations using the VHLSS, 2020. Legend series: Central Highlands; Midlands & Northern Mountains; Red River Delta; Mekong Delta; Northern & Coastal Central; Southeast. No values are printed; approximate readings (~, in millions):
- Red River Delta: 2010 ~19; 2012 ~19; 2014 ~20.5; 2016 ~21; 2018 ~21.5; 2020 ~24
- Northern & Coastal Central: 2010 ~17.5; 2012 ~17.5; 2014 ~17.5; 2016 ~18.5; 2018 ~20; 2020 ~20.2
- Mekong Delta: 2010 ~17.5; 2012 ~17.5; 2014 ~17.5; 2016 ~16.5; 2018 ~16.5; 2020 ~17
- Southeast: 2010 ~15; 2012 ~16; 2014 ~17; 2016 ~17; 2018 ~17; 2020 ~17.2
- Midlands & Northern Mountains: 2010 ~12.5; 2012 ~13.5; 2014 ~13; 2016 ~14.5; 2018 ~15.2; 2020 ~12.8
- Central Highlands: 2010 ~5.2; 2012 ~5.2; 2014 ~5.6; 2016 ~6; 2018 ~6.4; 2020 ~6
Pattern: Red River Delta rises fastest to the highest level, Northern & Coastal Central and Southeast also grow, while Midlands & Northern Mountains dips after 2018 and Central Highlands stays lowest with modest growth.

elements.label: Figure 3.4: Population distribution by region, 2020
elements.description: Pie chart titled "Number of households (in millions)". Slices with printed values: Central Highlands 1.5m; Mekong Delta 4.6m; Midlands & Northern Mountains 3.3m; Northern & Coastal Central 5.5m; Red River Delta 6.6m; Southeast 5.3m. Legend (two columns): Central Highlands; Mekong Delta; Midlands & Northern Mountains; Northern & Coastal Central; Red River Delta; Southeast. Pattern: Red River Delta is the largest slice, followed by Northern & Coastal Central and Southeast, while Central Highlands is the smallest.
